title: KENYA: Catholic Bishops Call for Protection of Migrant and Refugees’ Children
desc:
By Lorna Theuri
Kenya's Catholic bishops have called for the protection of refugee and migrant children in camps and cities across the country.
In a message issued on Sunday, 27th September, to mark the 112th World Day of Migrants and Refugees themed “Even Just One of These Children”, the Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops (KCCB), through the refugees, migrants and seafarer’s department, warned against exploiting the displaced persons.
The message drew on Pope Leo XIV's own World Day message, which urges the faithful to listen to each child's story, fears and dreams, and to resist reducing people to numbers. It said the Pope wants every child's dignity recognized before their status as a migrant.
The bishops said children at refugee centres should not be treated as a statistic in a report, a burden at a border, or a forgotten casualty of regional conflict.
The Bishops message said a society that honours human dignity must reject exploitation, neglect, trafficking and detention without protection. It described the day as not an optional expression of kindness, but a demand of faith. If even one child is left hungry, denied shelter, education or protection, or is trafficked, abused or abandoned, the bishops said, the Church's work remains unfinished.
They asked civil authorities and humanitarian partners to uphold the principle of the child's best interests and called on public and private institutions to protect children through effective legal instruments and family reunification, and to prevent the trauma of family separation.
The Bishops said that Kenya's national debate should move beyond mere migration management to the full protection of human rights, in the statement signed by Bishop Peter Munguti Makau, a member of the Institute of Consolata Missionaries (IMC), and Chairperson of KCCB’s Migrants, Refugees and Seafarers Department.
Referring to Pope Leo’s XIV's message for the international observance that was established by the Vatican, the Bishop said there is a need for a coordinated, supportive and effective response that guarantees protection, welcome and real opportunities for integration.
The Bishops also called for cooperation among faith communities, saying young people's vulnerability knows no religious boundaries. They said religious groups in Kenya should build networks of protection and shield children from extremist groups while respecting their cultural identity.
The message drew on Pope Leo XIV's own World Day message, which urges the faithful to listen to each child's story, fears and dreams, and to resist reducing people to numbers. It said the Pope wants every child's dignity recognized before their status as a migrant.
The Bishops cited the Holy Family's flight into Egypt and the parable of the Good Samaritan as models for the Church's response. They concluded with a prayer asking that refugees in Kenya be blessed with strength, healing, dignity, and peace.

title: Gabriele Grosso named 2026 Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation Experimental Physics Investigator
desc: Physicist Gabriele Grosso has been selected as one of 21 mid-career scientists to join the 2026 Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation’s Experimental Physics Investigators Initiative cohort. The five-year, $1.35 million award will allow Grosso and his lab to pursue an unconventional idea in quantum science: Instead of treating tiny vibrations inside materials as a problem to be eliminated, researchers will endeavor to put them to useful work.
